title: The Fortune Teller
text: An old woman with a deck of cards sits on a rock by the road, shuffling, though her eyes are sewn shut. She will read for one of you, for free. The cards, she says, are the price, and she smiles with too many teeth.

options.label: The Leader has their cards read, and pays whatever price the cards ask.

outcomes.text: She turns a card over, and it is not the one the Leader was born under. It is now, and it always will be.

options.label: The wisest listens from the edge, to learn how she does it.

outcomes.text: Every reading she gives is a little true. The wisest learns how she does it.

options.label: Pass her by. Anything she reads for free will cost you dearly.

outcomes.text: She laughs, and shuffles, and lays one card face up on the rock as you go: the Tower. You all walk faster after that.

options.label: The Soothsayer reads for her instead, and turns her own cards on her.

outcomes.text: She goes white at the third card, and pays them to stop.
